title: Helm chart changes for Private upgrade sequencing, readiness gates, and safe restart policy
creator: Ethan Park
description:
We need to update `redwood-helm-charts` to support the new Private upgrade controller/installer sequencing model.

This ticket covers chart-level mechanisms required for safe upgrades:
- deterministic ordering/guardrails across components (control plane, gateway, runtime, observability agents)
- explicit readiness gates before proceeding to next phase
- safe restart policy to avoid split-brain and reduce partial-outage windows
- backwards compatibility notes (existing installs + older installer versions)

Out of scope: implementing installer orchestration itself (ENG-2314) or rollback hooks contract (ENG-2318). This ticket focuses on chart hooks/jobs/templates/values that the installer can reliably call into.

Background
- Upgrade runs are driven by `redwood-private-installer` step graph (see PR references below). The installer needs stable, well-documented chart behaviors (hooks, timeouts, idempotency).
- We must reduce the probability of: gateway rolling before control plane readiness; schema migrations running without proper gates; pods restarting simultaneously leading to downtime.

Requirements
1) Upgrade sequencing primitives (Helm)
- Provide a pre-upgrade migration job (or hook) that can be invoked explicitly and blocks until completion.
- Provide a post-upgrade smoke test job (or hook) that validates control plane API readiness and basic request path health.
- Ensure ordering is deterministic and documented (control plane before gateway; schema migrations before runtime roll).

2) Readiness gates
- Add readiness probes/conditions that represent “safe to proceed to next phase”, not just container started.
- Explicitly gate gateway rollout on control plane health endpoint (avoid edge case from earlier staging rehearsal).
- Provide timeouts and clear failure messages (surface as Kubernetes job failures when possible).

3) Safe restart policy
- Reduce risk of split-brain during upgrades: orderly termination, preStop hooks, PDBs where appropriate.
- Avoid thundering-herd restarts: configure rolling update strategy and maxUnavailable defaults for critical components.
- Ensure migrations run as a singleton with concurrency policy.

4) Backwards compatibility
- Defaults must be safe for existing installs.
- Feature-flag hooks/jobs via values so older installers don’t accidentally trigger new behavior.
- Document minimum supported Helm version / Kubernetes version assumptions in chart NOTES and docs.

Acceptance criteria
- Chart supports explicit installer sequencing: installer can call `helm upgrade` without unexpected hook ordering changes.
- New hooks/jobs are idempotent (re-running after partial failure should not corrupt state; safe to re-run once service is stable).
- Gateway no longer rolls ahead of control plane readiness (validated in staging upgrade rehearsal).
- Backwards-compat documented in chart changelog and upgrade guide: values defaults, behavior changes, and opt-in flags.
- Add at least one integration test path in Private upgrade harness that validates gating behavior (coordinate with ENG-2322/PR harness).

Implementation plan (proposed)
A) Schema migration gating
- Add `control-plane-migrate` Job template.
- Prefer explicit job triggered by installer step (not purely Helm pre-upgrade hook), to keep sequencing deterministic in the installer step graph.
- If hooks are used, ensure weights and annotations are documented and consistent.

B) Post-upgrade smoke tests
- Add `post-upgrade-smoke` job that:
  - waits for control plane service endpoints
  - runs a minimal auth-less or service-token authenticated request against `/healthz` and `/readyz` (confirm exact endpoints with control plane team)
  - (optional) checks gateway route to control plane if available in VPC/private topology

C) Gateway readiness gate
- Add initContainer or startup gate that blocks gateway pods from becoming Ready until control plane `/readyz` passes.
- Add clear logging in init container when gate is failing (include DNS target, timeout).

D) Safe restart defaults
- For control plane + gateway:
  - rollingUpdate: maxUnavailable=0, maxSurge=1 (or equivalent) where feasible
  - add preStop to drain and allow in-flight requests to complete
  - ensure terminationGracePeriodSeconds is sufficient (coordinate with SRE)
- For runtime components:
  - preserve existing defaults where possible; do not over-constrain if it causes cluster scheduling failures

E) Values & flags
- Introduce values (names tentative; finalize with Release Eng):
  - `upgrade.enabled` (default false)
  - `upgrade.migrations.enabled` (default false)
  - `upgrade.smokeTests.enabled` (default false)
  - `upgrade.gatewayReadinessGate.enabled` (default false)
  - `upgrade.timeouts.*` to centralize job timeouts
- Add `NOTES.txt` to explain how installer uses these values and how operators should interpret failures.

Backwards compatibility notes (must be captured in chart CHANGELOG)
- All upgrade hooks/jobs are disabled by default.
- Enabling `upgrade.*` features may lengthen upgrade time due to explicit waits.
- If a customer has custom gateway values (readinessProbe, initContainers), we must avoid clobbering them; prefer additive templates and `tpl` merges where possible.
- If a cluster lacks permissions to run Jobs in namespace (locked-down RBAC), upgrade will fail earlier with actionable error.

Risks / gotchas
- Helm hooks can be surprising across versions; ensure we’re not relying on hook deletion policies that differ.
- Smoke tests must not require external connectivity in air-gapped mode.
- Readiness gate initContainer can deadlock if control plane DNS/service name changes; keep configurable via values and defaults.

References
- Linear: ENG-2314 (overall orchestration), ENG-2318 (rollback hooks contract), ENG-2315 (compat matrix enforcement)
- GitHub:
  - redwood-helm-charts PR-205: schema migration gating + post-upgrade smoke tests
  - redwood-helm-charts PR-212: values for backup targets/retention + feature-flagged rollback hooks
  - redwood-helm-charts PR-219: fix gateway rollout before control plane is ready (readiness gate + timeout tuning)
  - redwood-helm-charts PR-224: rollback annotations + pre-stop hooks

Test plan
- Staging Private environment:
  - run upgrade with `upgrade.*` flags enabled; validate sequencing: migrations -> control plane ready -> gateway rollout -> smoke tests
  - induce failure: break control plane readiness endpoint and verify upgrade blocks at gate with clear job failure output
- CI:
  - unit test templates with `helm template` snapshot for key values
  - add an e2e step in upgrade harness to assert that gateway pods do not become Ready before control plane readiness condition

Open questions
- Control plane endpoints: confirm exact readiness endpoint and auth requirements for smoke tests.
- Default timeouts: SRE to confirm baseline thresholds for migration and smoke tests (avoid false positives on slow clusters).
- Should we prefer initContainer gate vs. readinessProbe gate for gateway? (initContainer provides clearer blocking semantics, but can affect restart behavior).

comments: 2025-01-24 — Connor O’Brien: +1 to avoiding Helm pre-upgrade hooks as the primary sequencing mechanism. Installer step graph should remain the source of truth; use jobs as explicit steps. Hooks are OK for post-upgrade smoke tests if we can guarantee ordering, but I’d prefer explicit invocation as well for consistency.

2025-01-29 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): For safe restart policy, maxUnavailable=0 is good for control plane and gateway, but watch for smaller clusters where surge scheduling fails. Suggest maxSurge=1 with fallback to 0 if scheduling fails is not something Helm can do; we may need to document minimum headroom required when upgrade features enabled.

2025-02-03 — Michael Nguyen: Migration job must enforce singleton semantics. If using Job, set `parallelism: 1`, `completions: 1`, and consider `backoffLimit: 0` so failures are immediate and surfaced to installer. Also needs to write migration metadata (forward-only flags) but that’s handled in control plane; chart just needs to ensure job runs before API pods roll.
2025-02-06 — Ines Carvalho: Drafted values flags under `upgrade.*` and added NOTES text explaining opt-in. Working on making gateway gate additive (won’t overwrite customer-provided initContainers).

2025-02-10 — Ethan Park: Please ensure smoke test job does not depend on external DNS/egress. For on-prem, we’ll likely run against ClusterIP service. Also align endpoint path with control plane `/readyz` (tentative) and return codes.

2025-02-12 — Ines Carvalho: PRs opened/updated: PR-205 (migration gating + smoke tests), PR-219 (gateway readiness gate + timeouts), PR-224 (preStop + rollback annotations). Remaining: finalize changelog/backwards-compat section and add helm template snapshot tests.

2025-02-14 — Connor O’Brien: Marking as In Review pending Release Eng sign-off on values names and installer invocation. Need explicit note in changelog: upgrade features disabled by default; enabling will add jobs + extend upgrade duration.
